The buoyancy force $ F_{\text{buoy}} $ for an open-ended casing can be calculated using the following equation from **Textbook of Petroleum Engineering** (e.g., "Petroleum Engineering Handbook," 2nd Edition, Volume 2, Chapter 10):

$$
F_{\text{buoy}} = (P_e) \cdot (A_o - A_i)
$$

Where:
- $ P_e $ = external pressure = 2400 psi
- $ A_o $ = outside area = 18.0 in²
- $ A_i $ = inside area = 12.5 in²

### Calculation:
$$
F_{\text{buoy}} = 2400 \, \text{psi} \cdot (18.0 - 12.5) \, \text{in}^2 = 2400 \cdot 5.5 = 13,200 \, \text{lbf}
$$

### Final Answer:
$$
F_{\text{buoy}} = 13,200 \, \text{lbf}
$$

### Source:
**Petroleum Engineering Handbook**, 2nd Edition, Volume 2, Chapter 10 – "Casing Design and Buoyancy Calculations."
